finding.negative_quote: HSE request you do not seek an update on the status of your request before the statutory / recommended date for response has expired. finding.conduct: Automatic receipt for a request about 1988–89 demolition notifications. Before any work is done it asks the requester not to chase and warns that replies are not always sent within the statutory time.

terms.term: do not seek an update

chestnuts.title: Darwin Gray LLP (solicitors, Cardiff) · reply of 2026-11-02

finding.negative_quote: we have not seen any communication or document from you on that date. We have the enquiries you have sent to us on 19 and 21 September 2026 … we do not hold anything relating to this matter apart from what you have sent us, which you will be able to obtain from your own ‘sent items’ in your email account.
finding.trigger: Follow-up of 31 October 2026 from the enquirer, citing the preservation notice of 28 September 2026: was any file held, what searches were made, was anything destroyed or transferred, and a request that nothing be destroyed while the enquiries are open.
finding.conduct: The enquirer's Sent folder holds the preservation notice of 28 September 2026 (22:39 UK time), addressed to two of the firm's email addresses, one in To and one in Cc, with no delivery-failure notice for either; the firm's mail server had returned an immediate rejection for a different address on 21 September. Two further emails of 27 September and 7 October also went to the firm's general address. The reply of 2 November names only the enquiries of 19 and 21 September, states that the firm was founded in 2002, was never instructed about the land and holds nothing beyond the enquirer's own emails. It gives no account of a search of its mail system or quarantine for the 28 September notice, and no undertaking that nothing will be destroyed.

terms.term: have not seen any communication or document from you on that date
terms.statute: No delivery failure was recorded for either address; the notice's Message-ID can be traced in the firm's own mail logs. A UK GDPR Art. 15 subject access request (one month) covers every email from the enquirer the firm holds.

terms.term: we do not hold anything … apart from what you have sent us
terms.statute: UK GDPR Art. 15(1)(d): the retention period for the enquirer's own emails is not stated

terms.term: no preservation undertaking
terms.statute: A private firm has no FOIA s.77 duty; a duty to preserve arises for a likely party to proceedings (CPR PD 31B para 7; PD 57AD para 3.1); after a subject access request, DPA 2018 s.173 makes deletion to prevent disclosure an offence

chestnuts.title: bp (legal team, via a contractor) · reply of 2026-10-23

finding.negative_quote: we are not aware of any outstanding or live cause of action that bp or any related entity would need to answer in relation to this property. … we are not in a position to understand why a document preservation obligation would exist, and we are therefore not able to confirm that a preservation hold of the kind you describe will be put in place.
finding.trigger: Preservation notice of 16 October 2026 to a named bp lawyer, asking for a hold on records about the farm from 1969; it was passed to a contractor in the legal team.
finding.conduct: The first preservation notice, of 28 September 2026, went to BP Archive with no delivery failure and has had no reply; records enquiries of 19 and 29 October to the same address are also unanswered. The reply of 23 October answers the later notice of 16 October only, does not mention the 28 September notice, declines to confirm a preservation hold, finds many of the notice's links inaccessible and asks for the basis of any new case, the legal grounds and the relief sought. Follow-ups of 24 October (asking for hold confirmation by 7 November 2026) and 31 October had automatic out-of-office replies only, up to 2 November 2026.

terms.term: not able to confirm that a preservation hold … will be put in place
terms.statute: A party's duty to preserve arises once it knows it may become a party to proceedings (PD 57AD para 3.1; CPR PD 31B para 7); the reply ties the hold to the absence of a live cause of action

terms.term: not aware of any outstanding or live cause of action
terms.statute: Concluded litigation (Court of Appeal, 1987) cited as the reason no hold is needed; no statement of the company's retention schedule or of any destruction

terms.term: no reply to the notice of 28 September 2026
terms.statute: A company has no FOIA s.77 duty; a UK GDPR Art. 15 subject access request can ask for retention periods (Art. 15(1)(d))

chestnuts.title: Mount Stuart Trust (Bute Collection) · enquiry and automatic reply of 2026-10-15

finding.negative_quote: Please note that we are currently unable to respond to general external enquiries. We anticipate reviewing this position in January 2027. [...] Please note we are not able to respond to family history or genealogical enquiries at this time.
finding.trigger: Research-visit request from the enquirer, sent on 15 October 2026 at 23:01:51 UTC (00:01 on 16 October, UK time), asking for named Bute Estate (Glamorgan) records on Llandough-juxta-Penarth.
finding.conduct: The enquirer sent a research-visit request on 15 October 2026 at 23:01:51 UTC. The automatic reply came at 23:02:03 UTC the same day, 12 seconds later. It replied that general external enquiries are paused, with the position to be reviewed in January 2027 (a review date, not a date for answers), and that family history enquiries are not answered at this time. Research visits remain open by appointment three weeks ahead. Follow-ups sent on 19 October 2026 (22:14 UTC) and 29 October 2026 (19:55 UTC) have had no reply as of 3 November 2026; a further records request of 31 October 2026 has had no reply either. An earlier enquiry of 23 August 2026 went to a different address of the Trust and was returned undelivered (address not found).

terms.term: unable to respond to general external enquiries
terms.statute: A private trust: FOIA and the EIR do not apply, so no statutory deadline runs; the pause covers every general enquiry, whatever records it names

terms.term: reviewing this position in January 2027
terms.statute: No end date given: January 2027 is when the pause is to be reviewed, not when replies resume

terms.term: not able to respond to family history or genealogical enquiries
terms.statute: No statute applies to a private collection; a request about estate and title records is answered with the family history line

finding.chestnut: currently unable to respond to general external enquiries

chestnuts.title: Vale of Glamorgan Council · reply of 2026-11-10

finding.negative_quote: We are working through all your requests, including the internal review. We apologise once again that some are delayed in their response. Unfortunately due to the historic nature of the information you are seeking we have found this to be a bit problematic. Thank you for bearing with us and we shall be in further contact with you as soon as possible.
finding.trigger: Case 00211557 and new request 00211721, with an internal review of the council's handling outstanding; the reply of 10 November 2026 answers both under one case reference.
finding.conduct: One reply covers the whole caseload. It apologises that some replies are late, puts the difficulty down to the age of the material, and promises further contact without a date. It does not identify which requests are outstanding, how far behind each one is, or what has been searched, and it does not separate the new request from the internal review it answers in the same message. No statutory clock and no exception is mentioned.

terms.term: due to the historic nature of the information you are seeking
terms.statute: FOIA s.10(1) / EIR reg 5(2): 20 working days; the age of a record is not a ground for extension, and an EIR reg 7 extension needs complexity and volume notified inside the 20 days

terms.term: a bit problematic
terms.statute: FOIA s.16(1) / EIR reg 9: the duty to advise and assist; nothing states what would make the search possible or what the enquirer could narrow

terms.term: working through all your requests, including the internal review
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1) / EIR reg 5(1): each request is answered on its own terms, and an internal review has its own timetable under the s.45 Code of Practice

held_back: The signatory's name is withheld; the role title is given instead.

finding.negative_quote: We can certainly formally process your request for information under the Freedom of Information Act 2000, although it is not apparent to us that the Cabinet Office would hold: [...] Because of the broadness of this subject matter, we suspect that it would not be possible to determine whether any information within the scope of this request is held within the cost limit of £600 (calculated at £25 per hour). [...] If you are able to be more specific about what you are wanting then we may be able to assist.
finding.trigger: Request for any guidance, policy, procedure or central record on how inconsistent replies from different public authorities on the same subject are coordinated or referred between bodies.
finding.conduct: The reply neither confirms nor denies that such a record exists. It states that it is not apparent to the Cabinet Office that it would hold one, raises the £600 cost limit as a suspicion rather than as a decision, and invites a narrower request. No search account is given, no refusal notice is issued and no specific narrower scope is suggested. Because the cost limit is only floated, it carries no right of review, and the question whether any body coordinates such replies is left without a yes or a no.

terms.term: it is not apparent to us that the Cabinet Office would hold
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1)(a): the authority must state whether it holds the information, after a search; 'not apparent' is not a held or a not held answer

terms.term: within the cost limit of £600 (calculated at £25 per hour)
terms.statute: FOIA s.12(1) and s.17: the limit may be relied on only by a refusal notice that gives the estimate and the advice under s.16

terms.term: If you are able to be more specific about what you are wanting
terms.statute: FOIA s.16(1): the duty to advise and assist; the reply does not identify what narrower scope would fit inside the limit

finding.negative_quote: As a result, we consider your requests under ATISN 27589 to be substantially similar to those you previously made under ATISN 27021. [...] no further information is held by Welsh Government on any point contained in your request ATISN 27589.
finding.positive_quote: They all date from between 2006-2012 and are all marked for destruction under Welsh Government's Retention Schedules but, in acknowledgement of Part D of this request, this now has now been put on hold.
finding.positive_nature: register entries for four named files, and a hold placed on six files marked for destruction
finding.trigger: Preservation request of 28 September and 1 October 2026, and a request for the register entry, content dates and current status of the files named in the internal review of ATISN 27021; the section 14(2) refusal of ATISN 27589 was challenged on three points.
finding.disclosure_type: later disclosure of register detail and retention status; preservation outcome
finding.conduct: Two outcomes arrive in one letter. The earlier request is closed off as substantially similar to one already reviewed, with the enquirer sent to the Information Commissioner rather than to an internal review of that letter. In the same letter the Welsh Government supplies register detail it had not given before: four files with content dates, a retain-permanently value and a status of still held, and six Tir Gofal files dated 2006 to 2012, marked for destruction, whose destruction is now held while the requests remain open. The hold is the preservation outcome the enquirer asked for. The letter does not state what search produced the status of the six files, and its sentence recording the hold repeats a word in the original as sent.

terms.term: substantially similar to those you previously made
terms.statute: FOIA s.14(2): a repeated request may be refused, but the three new points in ATISN 27589 are then left unanswered, and the letter offers the Information Commissioner's route rather than an internal review of that refusal

terms.term: no further information is held by Welsh Government on any point
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1)(a) and s.16: the answer rests on three earlier emails of 10 July, 29 July and 27 August 2026, not on a fresh search of the records

terms.term: marked for destruction under Welsh Government's Retention Schedules ... put on hold
terms.statute: FOIA s.1 / EIR reg 5: a record scheduled for destruction that falls in scope still has to be identified and considered; a hold preserves it and does not answer the request

terms.term: you can ask for an internal review within 40 working days
terms.statute: FOIA s.45 Code of Practice Part VI: the review route and its timetable

held_back: The signatory's name is withheld; the role title is given instead.

chestnuts.title: Amgueddfa Cymru / Museum Wales · reply of 2026-11-18

finding.negative_quote: In undertaking searches for the information you have requested, we have encountered significant technical difficulties. Due to the volume of archived RCAHMW records held within our systems, identifying and searching the relevant material has proved more complex than anticipated. Attempts to extract information from the archive have also resulted in system stability issues, and our IT team is currently investigating alternative methods of carrying out the searches. As a result, we will not be able to provide a full response by today's deadline. We would therefore be grateful if you would agree to an extension until 2 December 2026
finding.trigger: Requests of 19 and 22 October 2026 under references 2026-024, 2026-032 and 2026-036, narrowed to collection and accession records for the c.1880 ironwork find at Great House Farm; this message arrived on the day the response was due.
finding.conduct: The extension is asked for on the deadline, in the message that reports the difficulty: the volume of archived records, and extraction from the archive causing system instability, with the IT team looking for other search methods. It asks for the enquirer's agreement rather than recording an extension taken, and gives 2 December 2026 as the new date. Nothing states what had been searched up to the deadline, and no reason is given why the difficulty could not have been reported earlier. The same thread four hours later records that the extension was authorised under delegated authority.

terms.term: we have encountered significant technical difficulties
terms.statute: EIR reg 7 / FOIA s.10(3): extra time needs complexity and volume, notified inside the 20 working days; technical difficulty is not itself a ground

terms.term: we would therefore be grateful if you would agree to an extension
terms.statute: FOIA s.10(3) / EIR reg 7: an extension is the authority's decision to take and notify, not a matter for the requester's consent; withholding consent does not stop the clock

terms.term: our IT team is currently investigating alternative methods
terms.statute: EIR reg 9 / FOIA s.16: the duty to advise and assist; nothing states how the records can be reached in the meantime

terms.term: until 2 December 2026
terms.statute: EIR reg 7: an extension must be for a stated period, with the reason given; a date is supplied without tying it to the reg 7 conditions

chestnuts.title: Amgueddfa Cymru / Museum Wales · reply of 2026-11-18

finding.negative_quote: The organisation does not consider it necessary, for the purposes of administering these requests, to identify individual members of staff involved in their handling.
finding.positive_quote: Responsibility for managing and determining Freedom of Information requests, including procedural matters such as extensions of time, sits with the Head of Governance under delegated authority. The extension previously notified in relation to these requests was authorised under that delegated authority. No separate managerial approval was required.
finding.positive_nature: the post that holds the authority is named, and the extension is confirmed as authorised
finding.trigger: The enquirer's email of 18 November 2026 asking for the name and job title of the member of staff who wrote, whether that person was the case handler or a duty manager, the manager with operational responsibility, and who authorised the extension.
finding.disclosure_type: procedural disclosure: the delegation under which the extension was authorised
finding.conduct: The reply moves the question from a person to a post. Responsibility for FOI handling and for extensions sits with the Head of Governance under delegated authority, and the extension was authorised under it without separate managerial approval. It then declines to identify individual staff. That answers the authorisation question, which is the part that bears on the extension, and leaves the identity of the individual unanswered by design. It also confirms the requests remain under consideration to the revised deadline.

terms.term: sits with the Head of Governance under delegated authority
terms.statute: FOIA s.45 Code of Practice: a public authority should say who is responsible for its FOI handling and its reviews; naming a post rather than an officer is consistent with the practice on junior staff

terms.term: does not consider it necessary ... to identify individual members of staff
terms.statute: FOIA s.40(2): personal data of staff would be the formal route for withholding names; no exemption and no public interest reasoning is set out

terms.term: No separate managerial approval was required
terms.statute: FOIA s.10(3) / EIR reg 7: whether an extension was properly authorised is a separate question from whether the conditions for taking one existed

chestnuts.title: The National Archives · internal review of 2026-11-18

finding.negative_quote: On 22nd September 2025, this record was included in a list of relocated records supplied to TNA, but we do not hold information on the precise date the relocation occurred. [...] No further information is held using the criteria provided on 13th August 2026.
finding.positive_quote: YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 forms part of the Parliamentary Archive collection made available at The National Archives between December 2025 and June 2026, following a large-scale relocation project.
finding.positive_nature: a dated account of the record's movement into the collection, not a newly located record
finding.disclosure_type: the movement of the record and the publication date of its catalogue entry
finding.trigger: Request of 13 August 2026 on the existence, provenance, transfer, retention, destruction or disposal of records relating to Ty Mawr / Great House Farm, and the internal review of the reply of 23 September 2026; the review addresses the relocation date of YHL/PO/JO/10/11/2536 and the date of its catalogue entry.
finding.conduct: The review confirms the record's movement. It forms part of the Parliamentary Archive collection made available between December 2025 and June 2026, the moves were managed by Parliament, and the record appeared on a relocation list supplied to The National Archives on 22 September 2025. The review then states that it holds no information on the precise date the relocation happened, and that 20 May 2026 is when the catalogue entry was published. It records that the reply of 23 September 2026 was a refusal notice, treats the later search terms as a new request and closes on the terms supplied in August. It also computes the handling time as 20 working days from receipt on 13 August 2026 to the final response on 23 September 2026; those two dates are just under six calendar weeks apart, and the review does not reconcile the difference. The identity of the reviewing officer is refused on the footing that junior civil servants are not named, and the Information Commissioner's postal address is given.

terms.term: included in a list of relocated records supplied to TNA
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1)(a): the holding question is answered, and the review identifies Parliament as the body that managed the moves

terms.term: we do not hold information on the precise date the relocation occurred
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1)(a): a not held answer should follow a search; the review does not state whether a deposit or transfer record was checked

terms.term: this review cannot consider or determine any new requests for information
terms.statute: FOIA s.45 Code of Practice Part VI: the review's scope is the original handling, so later search terms fall outside it

terms.term: 20 working days
terms.statute: FOIA s.10(1): the count runs from receipt; the review's own two dates of 13 August and 23 September 2026 do not produce 20 working days

terms.term: does not disclose the identities of junior civil servants
terms.statute: FOIA s.40(2): personal data of staff; the review cites a published policy page rather than the exemption

finding.negative_quote: Your Freedom of Information request regarding from 10 November 2026 EIR about Cardiff Corporation woodland and land records at Llandough / Leckwith, including the 29 March 1961 deed has been closed, as requested. Please submit a new request if you wish to obtain the information.
finding.trigger: EIR request FOI26599 about Cardiff Corporation woodland and land records at Llandough and Leckwith, including the 29 March 1961 deed, withdrawn on 19 November 2026.
finding.conduct: The reply is a closure notice, and it records the closure as made at the enquirer's request. It gives no account of any search, states nothing about what had been found before the request was withdrawn, and directs any future enquiry to a new request. Read with the withdrawal it answers, the thread ends the request rather than answering it, so the notice is not a refusal and not a not held answer. The wording also carries a stray word in the original as sent.

terms.term: has been closed, as requested
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1) / EIR reg 5(1): a request withdrawn by the requester ends the duty to answer, and no decision is recorded

terms.term: Please submit a new request if you wish to obtain the information
terms.statute: FOIA s.16 / EIR reg 9: nothing indicates whether any material was located before closure, so a new request begins from the start

chestnuts.title: National Library of Wales · reply of 2026-11-23

finding.negative_quote: For clarity, where we have previously stated "information not held", this related to information regarding the deaccessioning (removal) of these items from NLW. The information never existed since the items have not left NLW since their original accession to the collections. [...] All known item-level information has been provided therefore no further searches were required.
finding.positive_quote: Copies of the full catalogue records were not attached as they are publicly available online via the following links (this was an error on our part for which we apologise).
finding.positive_nature: a correction and explanation of the earlier not held answer, and the case reference put right
finding.disclosure_type: catalogue records; the scope of an earlier not held answer
finding.trigger: Request FOI/2026/17 for item-level records of the 1974 Report Wales holdings and for the search record behind earlier not held answers.
finding.conduct: The reply draws the line that the earlier answers left out: not held referred to records of deaccessioning, on the basis that the items have not left the Library, and no separate inspection record was created. It also states that no additional item-level records have been identified, that the correct reference is FOI/2026/17, that the earlier case numbers were administrative errors, and that catalogue records should have been attached. What it does not do is say whether any item-level record of the objects themselves was ever made. An object held but not digitised and a record never created are different things, and the reply answers the second.

terms.term: where we have previously stated "information not held"
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(1)(a) / EIR reg 12(4)(a): a narrowed answer; the reply attributes the earlier one to its scope rather than to a later search

terms.term: The information never existed since the items have not left NLW
terms.statute: FOIA s.1: a record never created is a different answer from a record not located, and neither is an exception to disclosure

terms.term: this was an error on our part for which we apologise
terms.statute: FOIA s.16 / EIR reg 9: correcting the supply of the catalogue records

terms.term: References to other case numbers in previous correspondence were administrative errors
terms.statute: FOIA s.45 Code of Practice: accuracy of case references in correspondence

finding.negative_quote: To ensure we withdraw the correct request, please can you confirm which of the two attached requests of 29 October 2026 you would like to withdraw. Separately, we note that an internal review of reference 260803049 is currently being processed. Please can you confirm if you would like to proceed with this.
finding.trigger: Withdrawal sent on 19 November 2026, answered by two questions: which of two requests of 29 October 2026 the withdrawal covers, and whether the internal review is to go on.
finding.conduct: A holding reply with two questions and nothing on the substance. It asks the enquirer to identify which of the two requests of 29 October 2026 is withdrawn, and separately whether the internal review should continue, and gives no date for either answer. The questions are the department's own record-keeping, and the internal review is recorded as being processed without a stated timetable. A role title is given and no individual is named.

terms.term: please can you confirm which of the two attached requests ... you would like to withdraw
terms.statute: FOIA s.1(3) / s.16: clarifying which request a withdrawal covers is not a clarification of scope, so the 20-working-day clock is unaffected

terms.term: an internal review ... is currently being processed
terms.statute: FOIA s.45 Code of Practice Part VI: no target date is given for the review's outcome
